Findings.Title: Public-boundary tests stop at the internal dispatcher
Findings.Evidence: The five disposition cases invoke Invoke-ReplMethod in process with Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn mocked. They do not execute Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 or Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 and do not assert actual child exit status or stdout/stderr separation. LastInvokeReplMethodSuccess is an internal flag, not process exit proof.
Findings.Impact: These cases can turn green while the public wrapper still swallows, duplicates, or contaminates the typed receipt or returns the wrong process result.
Findings.Remedy: Keep the dispatcher unit tests. Add isolated deterministic wrapper/child tests for the generic and Codex entry points with primary, queued and failed outcomes. Assert one parseable stdout receipt, diagnostics only on stderr, and exit 0 for primary/queued versus nonzero for rejected/lost. Exercise unchanged/stale-result behavior where the wrapper exposes it. No live server or integration tests are needed.

Findings.Title: Empty-output regression does not cover caller recovery behavior
Findings.Evidence: The case invokes Test-ReplTypedSessionMutationResult directly and asserts only Ok=false and a message. It never invokes the setTurnTitle or appendDialog workflows that consume this result and own retained recovery payloads.
Findings.Impact: An AllowEmptyString change alone can satisfy the helper test even if a caller throws, clears recovery data, publishes no rejection, or reuses stale success.
Findings.Remedy: Add workflow-level cases with transport Success=true and Output empty for setTurnTitle and appendDialog. Use isolated valid identity/freshness state; assert no unclassified exception, false/nonzero result, newly published rejected receipt for the current method/identity, and unchanged retained failsafe bytes. Seed an earlier primary receipt to reject stale-success reuse.
